object_description: long extruded structure with a continuous uniform profile
design_condition: The long structure occupies one side of the site to create a generous green area, but its scale and proximity to the surrounding streets reduce permeability, visual connections, and sensitivity to the existing trees.

positive.statement: The cleverly developed sectional figure is fascinating in its representative potential.
The main access arrangement naturally connects the building to the site and establishes clear spatial order.
The interconnected indoor and outdoor spaces promise daily added value for school life.
The entrance hall’s view of the gymnasium contributes to a specific spatial atmosphere.
Large contiguous areas with logical development offer scope for future change and a sustainable life cycle.
The architectural identity is impressive and the materialization is believable.

negative.statement: The building’s considerable dimension strains the site’s characteristic permeability and visual references.
Its extension into the street space affects surrounding trees and does not convincingly address the street.
The uniform height and structure require stronger differentiation to integrate into the district and gain social acceptance.
A single main entrance with long internal corridors may not provide a pleasant arrival for the whole school.
The uniform facade makes it difficult for children to identify and orient themselves at their entrances.
The roof-level outdoor spaces may not be sufficiently available to the district outside school hours.
The jury missed additional public leisure and play opportunities at ground level.
Running tracks and parking occupy an atmospheric arrival space that should instead provide quality of stay.
The functional areas appear monotonous, and further transversal crossings are needed to improve orientation and district connections.
The SKB bus route could intersect undesirably with schoolchildren’s movements.
Classrooms facing an inward courtyard without an outside view are criticized.
There is no clear arrival room for the SKB on the ground floor.
The revised circulation becomes too narrow around staircases and would cause considerable operational problems.
The absence of ground-level play options is a missed opportunity for the neighbourhood.
The large facade area, terraces and footprint weaken economic efficiency, ecology and generally accessible open space.
